body_markdown:
Hedley Studios, the British company that’s famed for its scaled-down classic cars, has partnered with Porsche on a[550 Spyder](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/porsche-550-spyder-unpacking-the-history-behind-a-thrilling-survivor-sports-car/) replica.


The legendary 1953 Porsche has been recreated at 80 percent scale, but with its type 547 *Fuhrmann* four-cylinder boxer engine swapped for electric power. In standard guise, there’s an 8 kW (11 hp) motor that delivers a top speed of 40 mph, but opt for the RS Pack and the output is doubled to 15 kW (22 hp), increasing the top speed to 50 mph. Driving range is 30 and 50 miles, respectively.


Known as the Porsche 550 J (for Junior), the car is clothed in lightweight carbon-fiber bodywork, with tooling created by 3D scanning 550 Spyders from the Porsche Museum. The 550 J weighs in at just 1168 lbs, or 1212 lbs in RS guise, and despite being only 114 inches long, there’s room for two adults to squeeze inside.


Hedley Studios


Underpinning the petite Porsche is a TIG-welded tubular spaceframe chassis modeled on the original car, with monotube Bilstein coilovers in lieu of twin-tube Fichtel and Sachs dampers for the trailing arm front, and swing-axle rear suspension. Braking is by Brembo monobloc calipers with vented discs, and the aluminum wheels wear Continental tires.


The first 550 J is finished in *Weißaluminium* , picked to most closely match the 1953 model, but customers have a limitless choice of colors, including the full range of Paint-to-Sample options. The interior, which features bucket seats and a Nardi steering wheel, can of course be trimmed as desired. Neat touches include the repurposing of the 550’s choke lever as a drive mode selector, and turning the fuel gauge into a battery meter.


Hedley Studios


Hedley Studios


“The Porsche 550 Spyder is far more than a legendary sports car,” says Deniz Keskin, Porsche’s Director of Brand Management & Partnerships. “It embodies the pioneering spirit, innovative strength and passion that have defined Porsche from the brand’s earliest days to the present. The Porsche 550 J celebrates this unique heritage and brings the story of one of the most significant sports cars in our company’s history back to life in a contemporary and inspiring way.”


Only 250 Porsche 550 Js will be built, priced from around $94,000 plus taxes. It joins the[Bugatti Baby II](https://www.hagerty.com/media/driving/zipping-through-willow-springs-in-bugatti-baby-ii/) ,[Ferrari Testarossa J](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ferrari-testarossa-junior-no-toy/) ,[Aston Martin DB5J](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-look-review-aston-martin-db5-junior/) and[Bentley Blower Jnr](https://www.hagerty.com/media/driving/brilliant-blower-junior-brings-out-the-best-of-w-o-bentleys-london/) in[Hedley Studios](https://hedleystudios.com/) ‘ little car collection.
